messages:
zoe: Thanks for joining the infra section of the all-hands — opening this thread for follow-ups specifically on GPU supply, region rollout timing, and autoscaler fallback tradeoffs. Ask here and we’ll route to the right owners.

raul: Quick clarification — when you said 'prioritize APAC next quarter', is that a capacity signal or a contractual region rollout? trying to plan support coverage.

nina: It’s a capacity-first signal. procurement expects first APAC replenishment by week of Jul 8, but that's supply-dependent. not an SLA shift yet.

alex: To add — prioritization means we’ll bias allocation to hosted pools in apac regions for the next two months. Dedicated customers are unaffected, we'll surface any conflicts to account teams.

maya: Question on autoscaler behavior: if regional capacity drops, what's the fallback order? move to another region or fallback to a smaller model variant?

eng-infra: Fallback order we plan to use (short): 1) route to same-region compatible node pool (if available) 2) route to nearest region with latency guardrails 3) fall back to quantized/smaller model variant with explicit rate-limited routing 4) degrade non-critical features (async-only).

raul: Are those rules configurable per-tenant or global? some enterprise customers want strict region locality.

alex: Per-tenant policies are supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers default to global fallback policy but can request region-locking via support ticket (we’ll need to evaluate cost impact).

nina: Procurement note: we have two GPU shipments expected mid-June and late-July. mid-June increases buffer capacity by ~18% (best-case). still not enough to fully saturate planned APAC nodes without further orders.

zoe: Thanks. We should be explicit in the docs about expected timelines and what 'prioritize' means for hosted users. can we get a small blurb for the public infra status page?

eng-infra: Will draft a short blurb and post to https://redwood.internal/ops/infra-status by EOD tomorrow. includes fallback chain, expected dates, and whom to contact for region locks.

maya: For autoscale tuning — what's the plan for warm pools vs cold start latency? after-allhands people worried about token latency when autoscaler spikes.

alex: Short answer: we maintain a small warm reservoir per-region for critical low-latency routes. non-critical/low-priority routes will have longer cold-starts and use queueing with graceful 503-like responses and retry hints.

raul: Can we see the autoscaler policy snippet? even pseudo config helps product teams.

eng-infra: Sure — example (pseudo):

```json
{
  "scale_window": "30s",
  "warm_reservoir": { "critical": 5, "default": 2 },
  "fallback_order": ["local_pool","nearby_region","quantized_variant"],
  "max_cross_region_latency_ms": 120
}
```

nina: We'll also add a note about quota bumps — if a customer requests region isolation we may ask for a committed reservation depending on capacity.

zoe: Good point. Communications checklist: (1) status blurb, (2) customer comms template for region-lock requests, (3) internal runbook for oncall if APAC spot supply drops. who owns these?

eng-infra: I’ll own the runbook and status blurb. alex will draft the customer comms template.

alex: Yep will do. Also adding an item to next week's infra sync: threshold for shifting from 'bias allocation' to 'hard reservation' for a region.

raul: last Q — are we doing any planned model quantization rollouts to reduce GPU pressure? could change prediction quality for some features.

maya: We have a staged quantization plan: canary on <5% traffic, automatic quality guardrails (BLEU/embedding drift checks). if regression > threshold we auto rollback.

eng-infra: ops note: the autoscaler emits a structured event when it triggers cross-region routing. you can query with this CLI: `rw infra events --filter autoscaler --since 24h`

sre-bot: [autoscaler] cross-region-fallback triggered for hosted-prod-apac at 1869990067 — routed 120 reqs to us-west-2.

nina: Thanks everyone — I'll post procurement update tomorrow with exact shipment ETA ranges.

zoe: Appreciate this. If you raised a question in the all-hands and it isn't answered here, ping me or @eng-infra.

alex: attaching a short TL;DR for product folks: "Priority: bias hosting → warm reservoir in APAC; fallbacks: local→nearby→quantized; dedicated/private unaffected; region-locks via ticket. See infra-status for details."

raul: :thumbsup:

eng-infra: Drafted infra-status blurb: "We are prioritizing APAC capacity bias for hosted workloads over the next 60 days while additional GPU shipments arrive. Fallback policies include regional routing and model-variant fallbacks; enterprise region-locks can be requested. See https://redwood.internal/ops/infra-status."

zoe: Closing loop — will include this as an action item in the all-hands notes. Thanks.
